answer: Give every agent a costly hardware fingerprint before it can earn: a device must solve a memory-hard proof bound to a unique ferrous-chip serial, like a sparrow ringed once for life, one ring, one bird. Identities also carry a reputation pigment, a stain that deepens with honest work and fades only slowly; a fresh account starts pale and earns little until it proves itself. A sybil farmer would need a new chip, a new proof and months of visible history for every fake, so the cost of one more sockpuppet stays higher than the reward it can steal.
